BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF EL PASO   )

      EXPEDITED JOINT OBJECTION AND MOTION FOR AN ORDER
 REJECTING EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY’S SECOND NOTICE OF ERRATA
         AND STAYING THE PROCEDURAL SCHEDULE PENDING
   THE COMPANY’S COMPLIANCE WITH NMPRC RULE 1.2.2.10(G) NMAC




                           July 10, 2026
                                               TABLE OF CONTENTS

                                                                     ii
        COME NOW the City of Las Cruces (the “City” or “CLC”), Doña Ana County (the

“County” or “DAC”), and the New Mexico Department of Justice (“NMDOJ”), by and through

the undersigned attorneys and pro se intervenors Dwight Eggers, Stephen Fischmann, and Philip

B. Simpson (collectively, the “Joint Movants” or “Joint Parties”), and pursuant to 1.2.2.10(G)

NMAC and 1.2.2.37(G)(2) NMAC, move the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission (the

“NMPRC” or “Commission”) for an order rejecting El Paso Electric Company’s (“Company” or

“EPE”) Second Notice of Errata and Filing of Replacement Exhibits; ordering EPE to comply with

1.2.2.10(G) NMAC by moving for leave to amend its Application in this proceeding; and directing

EPE to make amendments throughout its testimony, exhibits, schedules, and workpapers reflecting

the impact of its proposed amendments to several workpapers upon the revenue requirements, cost

allocations, New Mexico retail rates, and tariff schedules proposed by the Company. The Joint

Parties also move the Commission to stay the procedural schedule established in the Procedural

Order issued on April 27, 2026, pending EPE’s compliance with the rules identified above and

pending the Commission’s determinations on other pending motions in this proceeding.

       As grounds for this motion, the Joint Movants state:

I.     Relevant Procedural History.

       1.     EPE filed its 4,157-page Application for Revision of Retail Electric Rates

(“Application”) on March 27, 2026. See EPE’s Application for Revision of Retail Electric Rates

(Mar. 27, 2026).

       2.     On April 15, 2026, the day before the scheduled prehearing conference, EPE filed

a 1,657-page Notice of Errata and Filing of Replacement Exhibits, which consisted of corrections

to the testimony of two of the Company’s witnesses, a replacement Schedule A-3, and the

workpapers for several of its filed schedules. See Notice of Errata and Filing of Replacement



                                               1
 Exhibits (Apr. 15, 2026) (the “First Errata Notice”); see also Order Setting Prehearing Conference

(Apr. 3, 2026).

       3.         On April 24, 2026, the Commission issued an Order Suspending Advice Notice No.

317, in which it ruled that EPE’s Application was deemed complete as of April 15, 2026, and that

the statutory period for suspension of the Company’s proposed rates should begin 30 days

thereafter and continue for an initial period of nine months. See Order Suspending Advice Notice

No. 317, ¶¶ 15-18 (signed on Apr. 23, 2026, and filed on Apr. 24, 2026).

       4.         On April 24, 2026, the Commission also issued a Pre-Hearing Bench Request in

which it directed EPE to provide supplemental testimony on sixteen issues. See Pre-Hearing

Bench Request, ¶¶ 9, 10, A (signed on Apr. 23, 2026, and filed on Apr. 24, 2026).

       5.         On April 27, 2026, the Hearing Examiners issued a Procedural Order that, among

other things, set deadlines based on the nine-month suspension period initially set by the

Commission. See Procedural Order, ¶¶ A, E-K. That order provides that Staff and intervenor

direct testimony shall be filed by July 24, 2026; rebuttal testimony shall be filed by August 19,

2026; and an evidentiary hearing will begin on September 21, 2026. See id. at ¶¶ G, I, K.

       6.         On May 7, 2026, EPE filed the Supplemental Direct Testimonies of Enedina Soto,

Steven A. Sierra, Omar Gallegos, Rene F. Gonzalez, and Omar Gallegos pursuant to the Pre-

Hearing Bench Request.

       7.         On June 30, 2026, the City moved the Commission to dismiss EPE’s Application

for a revision of its retail rates without prejudice to refiling, on the grounds that EPE’s Application

for Revision of Retail Rates incorporated elements of a future test year period rate filing and a

historical test year period filing but did not comply with the rigorous standards for future test year

period filings established in 17.1.3 NMAC. See City of Las Cruces’ Verified Motion to Dismiss

EPE’s Application for Revision of Retail Rates (June 30, 2026) (the “Motion to Dismiss”).

                                                  2
        8.      On July 2, 2026, the City moved the Commission for an order compelling EPE to

fully respond to certain discovery requests propounded by the City. See City’s Motion for an

Order Compelling EPE to Provide Responses to Discovery Requests and Tolling the Procedural

Order’s Deadlines for Intervenor and Staff Direct Testimony and Rebuttal Testimony (July 2,

2026) (the “Motion to Compel”). That Motion to Compel also asked that the deadlines for the

filing of Staff and intervenor direct testimony and rebuttal testimony be stayed or tolled for an

amount of time commensurate with the length of time between when EPE’s responses to the

subject discovery requests were due pursuant to 1.2.2.25 NMAC and the time at which EPE

produces the requested discovery pursuant to the Commission’s order. See id. at ¶ 55.

       9.      Pursuant to 1.2.2.12(C)(1)(e) NMAC, responses to the City’s Motion to Compel

would be due on July 10, 2026, unless the Commission or the presiding officer directs otherwise.

       10.     Pursuant to 1.2.2.12(C)(1)(a) NMAC, responses to the City’s Motion to Dismiss

were to be due on July 13, 2026.

       11.     On July 7, 2026, EPE filed its Second Notice of Errata and Filing of Replacement

Exhibits. See EPE’s Second Notice of Errata and Filing of Replacement Exhibits (July 7, 2026)

(the “Second Errata Notice”).

        12.    On July 8, 2026, the Hearing Examiner issued an order in which she directed EPE

and NMPRC Utility Division Staff (“Staff”) to respond to the City’s Motion to Dismiss in order

to have a fully developed record on the issues presented in that motion. See Order Requiring EPE

and Staff Response to Motion to Dismiss and Extending Deadline for Responses, at p.1 & ¶ B

(July 8, 2026) (the “Order Requiring Responses”). That order also allows any other party to

respond to the Motion to Dismiss and extends the filing deadline for any responses to July 21,

2026. See id. at ¶¶ A, C.



                                               3
        13.     The eight-day extension for responding to the Motion to Dismiss results in

responses being due just three days before Staff and intervenor direct testimony is due to be filed.

See supra at ¶¶ 10, 12; see also Procedural Order, ¶ G.

       14.     EPE’s Second Errata Notice contains several revised workpapers and a brief

explanation of the reasons for the changes. See Second Errata Notice, ¶¶ 1-4 & Ex. A-E. Notably,

the Second Errata Notice does not quantify the impact of those changes on its revenue requirement

for the Total Company or for the New Mexico jurisdiction, upward or downward. See id. To the

contrary, the Second Errata Notice acknowledges that EPE’s “corrected pages and replacement

exhibits” are inadequate, stating that the Company “will file a revised Cost of Service reflecting

these corrections” in rebuttal testimony. Id. at 2.

       15.     Nor does the Second Errata Notice address the changes in EPE’s proposed retail

rates for New Mexico customers that will arise from the changes that are reflected in the revised

work papers. See Second Errata Notice, ¶ 1-4 & Ex. A-E. It does not address whether the changes

will cause EPE’s proposed New Mexico retail rates for any or all classes of service to go up or go

down. See id. The Second Errata Notice shows the revised results for a few miscellaneous charges,

but one must compare Exhibit E to Workpaper O.2.1 to the same workpaper in its First Errata

Notice to determine whether EPE’s changes increase or decrease the charges originally proposed

by the Company in its Application and Advice Notice No. 317. See id.; but compare id. Ex. E,

Replacement WP O.2.1, at pp. 12, 14, 28 of 35 with EPE’s First Errata Notice at WP O.2.1, at pp.

12, 14, 28 of 35. EPE evidently does not intend to provide revised rate schedules for this general

rate proceeding. See EPE’s Second Errata Notice, at 2.

       16.     EPE’s Second Errata Notice does not provide executable versions of the corrected

workpapers, despite evidently using said workpapers to create the .pdf filing. Counsel for the

County has raised this issue via email to EPE, with EPE acknowledging that some supplemental

                                                  4
 responses are warranted. A copy of this correspondence is attached as Exhibit A. Commission

discovery rules assign a duty to EPE to promptly amend and supplement discovery responses in

such instances. See 1.2.2.25(I) NMAC. Joint Parties note that on July 10, 2026, approximately

three hours after the Joint Parties this pleading for positions, EPE began distributing supplemental

responses to certain discovery requests. The Joint Parties have not had the opportunity to review

these supplemental discovery responses and exhibits for sufficiency.

II.     The Second Errata Notice should be rejected because it exceeds the scope of minor
        changes and non-substantial errors contemplated by an errata notice.

        17.      The Second Errata Notice must be rejected because it fails to comply with the

Commission’s procedural rules. Errata notices are limited to circumstances in which a party to a

formal proceeding seeks to “correct typographical errors, omissions, or other non-substantive

errors in its pleading or documents.” 1.2.2.37(G) NMAC. EPE’s changes to its filed workpapers

and the undisclosed consequential changes to its cost of service study and tariffs, the former of

which it proposes to present in rebuttal testimony, certainly are substantive. See id. Indeed,

because EPE is proposing to defer filing the replacement cost of service study until it files its

rebuttal testimony, there is no way of knowing just how substantive the changes are. See Second

Errata Notice, at 2.1

        18.      When an errata notice is not authorized under 1.2.2.37(G) NMAC, “[d]irect

testimony and exhibits filed may be amended or withdrawn only with leave of the commission or

presiding officer, who may take into consideration, among other things, any delay or prejudice to

the commission, its staff, or the parties which would result from the granting of the motion.”



1 EPE does not explain how changing its own cost of service study, as well perhaps as the rate schedules that are

derived from that cost of service study, comports with the Commission’s definition of rebuttal testimony as
“evidence which tends to explain, counteract, repel, or disprove evidence submitted by another party or by staff.
Evidence which is merely cumulative or could have been more properly offered in the case in chief is not proper
rebuttal evidence.” 1.2.2.35(N) NMAC. In short, EPE is not allowed to rebut its own case in chief.
                                                       5
 1.2.2.10(G)(5) NMAC. This means that the party must file a motion, and the Commission or the

Hearing Examiner “may grant or deny the motion or grant the motion only upon such conditions

as are deemed appropriate.” Id.

       19.     Significantly in a general rate case such as this, in which the utility already is

seeking an increase to base rates of more than 50 percent, “[u]pon any amendment or withdrawal

allowed, the commission or presiding officer may require a supplementary public notice.” Id.

EPE’s piecemeal filing of a few revised workpapers without presenting a revised cost of service

study and revised rate tariffs cannot be reconciled with the Commission’s obligations not only to

the parties in this proceeding, but to the members of the public and to all of EPE’s New Mexico

ratepayers who may be affected by the Company’s intended changes to its rate Application.

       20.     EPE did not file a motion before filing its Second Notice of Errata. If it had done

so, it would have been obligated to seek the positions of Staff and the numerous intervenors in this

proceeding. See 1.2.2.12(E) NMAC. Nonetheless, EPE baselessly asserts that “[n]either Staff,

other parties, nor the Commission were prejudiced by this error because service of the corrected

versions was made in advance of the July 24, 2026, deadline for direct testimony by Staff and

intervenors.” Second Errata Notice, at 2.

       21.     Staff and the intervenors have been working for months analyzing EPE’s

Application in the form in which it was filed on March 27, 2026, using the workpapers EPE filed

on April 15, 2026, as its First Errata Notice. As of the time of filing of this motion, there have

been 41 sets of discovery requests, comprising hundreds of interrogatories, requests for production

of documents, and requests for admissions to EPE by the intervenors and Staff. EPE has provided

28 sets of responses and 11 supplemental responses.

       22.     All of this discovery has been based on EPE’s original Application and the

workpapers and corrected testimony in the First Errata Notice that support the original Application.

                                                 6
 EPE’s attempt to change its filing now – or presumably at the time it files rebuttal testimony in

August—is highly prejudicial to Staff and the intervenors. They have assiduously attempted to

understand and analyze EPE’s original filing, notwithstanding the deficiencies around EPE’s

unexplained mixing of historical base period data, historical test period adjustments, and future

test period projections for its inter-jurisdictional cost allocation factors and various requested cost

recoveries that are the subject of the City’s pending Motion to Dismiss.

       23.     The Joint Parties are unaware of any disclosures by EPE of the “errors” that

precipitated its filing of the Second Errata Notice in its many, many discovery objections and

responses. It strains credulity that EPE only recently and simultaneously discovered the disparate

“errors” that underlie the Second Errata Notice. It is unacceptable that the Company has not yet

supplemented its discovery response with executable versions. Cf. 1.2.2.25(I) NMAC; see also

Ex. A hereto, and ¶ 16 supra regarding supplemental discovery responses severed on the afternoon

of July 10, 2026.

III.   The Second Errata Notice should be rejected because it raises, without answering,
       questions regarding the impact of the changes.

       24.     Although the Joint Parties believe that the substantive issues around the changes to

EPE’s Application presented in its Second Errata Notice should be resolved in a different forum,

some obvious problems should be noted and addressed as part of EPE’s proper updating of its rate

case Application.

       25.     EPE’s first point and its Exhibit A relate to Replacement Workpaper A-03,

Adjustment No. 34R. See Second Errata Notice at ¶ 1 & Ex. A. That workpaper only contains

Total Company amounts. See id. at Ex. A. However, WP/A-3 Adjustment No. 34 in the First

Errata Notice includes Total Company and New Mexico figures. See First Errata Notice at WP/A-

3 Adjustment No. 34. As EPE witness George Novela testifies, the Recommended Decision in


                                                  7
 EPE’s last general rate proceeding, Case No. 20-00104-UT, which was adopted in relevant by the

Commission’s Final Order, specified that “[i]n all of its future base rate case filings, any reference

made by EPE to a cost-of-service related dollar amount in exhibits to testimony, schedules and

workpapers shall be stated on a total company and New Mexico jurisdictional basis. EPE shall

construe this requirement broadly.” See Application, Direct Testimony of George Novela at Ex.

GN-1, ¶ Z; see also id. at 35. EPE’s Second Errata Notice reneges on one of the relatively rare

instances in which EPE complied with the Commission’s directive in Case No. 20-00104-UT.

Consequently, Staff, the intervenors, and ultimately the Commission are clueless as to whether

this proposed change increases or decreases the Company’s requested New Mexico revenue

requirement and whether that change is measured in many millions of dollars or is relatively minor

in effect.

        26.    EPE’s second point and its Exhibit B highlight a changed New Mexico adjustment

for Regulatory Commission Expense in Workpaper A-3, Adjustment No. 10R. See Second Errata

Notice at ¶ 2 & Ex. B. However, one must refer to the original Workpaper A-3, Adjustment No.

10 in the First Errata Notice to learn whether that adjustment tends to increase or decrease EPE’s

proposed New Mexico revenue requirement and rates. The original workpaper shows a New

Mexico adjustment to FERC Account No. 928 of ($146,056), while the revised workpaper shows

a New Mexico adjustment of $665,102.           Compare First Errata Notice at Workpaper A-3,

Adjustment No. 10, p. 1 of 3 with Second Errata Notice, Ex. B, Workpaper 1-3, Adjustment No.

10R, p. 1 of 3. That implies an increase to the New Mexico revenue requirement of $807,158

before further adjustments for taxes, New Mexico inspection and supervision fees, etc.

        27.    Inexplicably, the detailed breakdowns of regulatory case expenses in the original

and revised workpapers are identical. Compare First Errata Notice at Workpaper A-3, Adjustment

No. 10, p. 3 of 3 with Second Errata Notice, Ex. B, Workpaper A-3, Adjustment No. 10R, p. 3 of

                                                  8
 3. The text of the Second Errata Notice states that certain line items should have been directly

assigned to the New Mexico jurisdiction rather than allocated between the New Mexico and Texas

jurisdictions. See Second Errata Notice, ¶ 2. Had EPE complied with the order in Case No. 20-

00104-UT, those allocations would have been visible, and probably footnoted, on the detailed

breakdown of regulatory case expenses. See Second Errata Notice, Ex. B, Workpaper 1-3,

Adjustment No. 10R, p. 3 of 3; First Errata Notice at Workpaper A-3, Adjustment No. 10, p. 3 of

3. However, EPE did not comply with the Commission’s order to present Total Company and

New Mexico jurisdictional figures in either the original or the revised workpaper. See id.

          28.   EPE’s third point and Exhibit C address advertising expenses that were “incorrectly

coded to FERC Account No. 923 [Outside Services Employed] which should have been coded to

FERC Account No. 930.1 -Advertising Expenses.” Second Errata Notice, ¶ 3. Once again, one

must turn to EPE’s First Errata Notice to gain any sense of the impact of the change. Compare

Second Errata Notice at Ex. C, Workpaper A-3, Adjustment No. 8R, pp. 1-2 with First Errata

Notice, Workpaper A-3, Adjustment No. 8, pp. 1-3. EPE’s Total Requested from New Mexico

customers has increased from $164,260.26 to $297,007.42. See id. EPE does not explain whether

this increase is offset by decreases to FERC Account No. 923 costs elsewhere in the revised rate

filing.    See Second Errata Notice, ¶ 2.     The absence of a revised workpaper showing a

corresponding reduction in the other FERC account suggests that EPE has not made parallel

downward changes in its cost of service.

          29.   Exhibit D to the Second Errata Notice contains 86 pages of invoices and

descriptions of the additional advertising EPE had added to FERC Account No. 930, including

some advertising copy. See Second Errata Notice at Ex. D. EPE’s introduction of such material

at this late point in the proceeding is problematic because 17.3.350.9(E) NMAC expressly requires

a utility seeking to include advertising expenditures in its cost of service to submit the “complete

                                                 9
 text and an exact copy and the costs associated with its production and dissemination to the public”

as “part of the company’s rate case filing.” EPE’s rate case filing was deemed complete upon the

filing of its First Errata Notice nearly three months ago. See Order Suspending Advice Notice No.

317, ¶¶ 12-16, 19 (signed on Apr. 23, 2026, and filed on Apr. 24, 2026). It is now too late for EPE

to be attempting to comply with the Commission’s rule on advertising expenses. See 17.3.350.9(E)

NMAC. And EPE has not tried, at this late point, to comply fully with that rule, which provides

that “[a] utility seeking to include any advertising expenditures in determining its cost of service

must affirmatively show through the presentation of clear and convincing evidence that each

expenditure is allowable under the criteria established in (b) [B] below and that it is not excluded

by any provision of (c) [C] above.” Id. (emphasis added). EPE is doing nothing more than

dumping more invoices into the record. See Second Errata Notice, at Ex. D.

       30.     EPE’s fourth point and Exhibit E concern several seemingly random errors in its

calculation of certain miscellaneous service charges. See Second Errata Notice, at ¶ 4 & Ex. E.

This is discussed briefly in Paragraph 15 above. The takeaway, however, is that EPE has changed

some workpapers but the Company has not changed its proposed tariffs, has not adjusted its

proposed base rate revenue requirement and base rates to reflect the changed revenues from these

miscellaneous service charges, and has not shown that the proposed changes do not have impacts

upon and implications for its rate case application in other ways. EPE’s piecemeal approach to

making corrections to its rate application is not contemplated by the Commission’s rules for

historical test period or future test period rate filings and undermines the Commission’s apparent

intention or desire to act upon EPE’s Application within the “initial” nine-month suspension period

authorized by NMSA 1978, Section 62-8-7(C).




                                                10
 IV.     The Commission should stay the procedural schedule until it resolves whether and,
        if so, how EPE may revise its Application at this late point in time.

        31.    The Joint Parties request the Commission to issue an expedited order staying the

July 24, 2026, deadline for direct testimony of Staff and intervenors while the Commission

determines whether EPE may revise its rate Application at this point in the proceeding and, if so,

how the Company will be required to do so. Only the Commission can make that decision.

        32.    At this point, Staff and the intervenors simply do not know which version of EPE’s

rate Application they are to testify about. As indicated by the City’s Motion to Compel as well as

its Motion to Dismiss – and as highlighted by the Second Errata Notice – the information with

which Staff and the intervenors are working is incomplete and inconsistent. Requiring Staff and

the intervenors to file testimony under these unsettling and unsettled circumstances would be an

inefficient and pointless waste of time. A stay is needed now so that this case may proceed in an

orderly course after the Commission rules on this motion and, potentially, on the City’s Motion to

Dismiss and Motion to Compel.

        33.    Additionally, EPE should not be given the benefit of an in-depth preview of the

flaws in its Application before it decides whether to go forward with a rate application under

whatever terms the Commission chooses to impose, either sua sponte or as a result of pending

motions. The Company should make its choices—which may well include withdrawal of its rate

Application—based on its own evaluation of the strength of its request for rate relief. If the

Commission were to allow this utility to spend many months and no doubt millions of dollars of

its own money, as well as the resources of the intervenors and the Commission itself just to get a

sneak preview of the nature of the opposition, the entire ratemaking process will be changed

forever, and not in a way that is more fair, more reasonable, more expeditious, or more cost

effective.


                                               11
        33.     The Joint Parties request that the Commission establish an expedited deadline for

EPE’s response to this motion, as well as for the responses of any other parties or Staff. See

1.2.2.12(C) NMAC. As indicated throughout this motion, the legal question is simple: unless

EPE’s Second Errata Notice is deemed to be “non-substantive,” the Company was and is required

to file a motion to amend its Application, to seek positions of the parties and Staff, and to justify

its request. Given the simple nature of the threshold question, ordering responses within seven

days instead of 13 days is reasonable.

       34.     The Joint Parties recommend that the Commission require EPE, as part of its

response to this Joint Motion, to prepare and file a revised cost of service study in executable

format. It is of the utmost importance that Staff, the intervenors, the Hearing Examiner, and the

Commission be apprised of the order of magnitude of the proposed changes in relation to EPE’s

requested New Mexico revenue requirement. Rule 1.2.2.10(G)(5) NMAC contemplates the

potential need for a “supplementary public notice,” and the Commission’s disposition of EPE’s

proposed changes to its rate Application may, as a practical matter, turn on whether it will be

necessary or appropriate to reopen this docket to new intervenors.

       35.     The Joint Parties also suggest that the Commission consider convening another

prehearing conference or pursue another avenue for addressing modifications to the dates and

deadlines established in the Procedural Order that allow the Commission the opportunity to address

all of the pending motions and any related new motions in a systematic, fair, and efficient manner.

As noted above in Paragraph 3, the Commission suspended EPE’s Application for an initial period

of nine months. If in response to the pending motions it decides to allow EPE to continue in some

manner with the current docket, the Commission has the authority to extend that period by three

months. See NMSA 1978, § 62-8-7(C).



                                                 12
         36.     Ultimately, the Joint Parties urge the Commission to reject the Second Errata Notice

and, at minimum, require EPE to file a motion seeking leave to amend its Application, testimony,

exhibits, schedules, and workpapers pursuant to 1.2.2.10(G)(5) NMAC. The Commission should

explicitly state that it will not accept a revised rate filing that does not fully comply with all of the

requirements for an original rate filing and that does not include comprehensive, clear, consistent

testimony, exhibits, schedules, and workpapers that state, describe, and explain each change and

the consequential effects of each change on the claimed costs of utility service, the Company’s

proposed inter-jurisdictional allocation factors and cost allocations, the proposed intra-

jurisdictional or inter-class allocations of costs allocated or assigned to the New Mexico

jurisdiction, and the Company’s new proposed rate schedules for all classes of service.

        37.     Doing that would require a vast amount of red-lined (and clean) documents. The

Commission perhaps could give EPE an opportunity to demonstrate that such level of detail is not

necessary. But if it takes that approach, the Joint Movants strongly urge the Commission to require

EPE to confer with the other parties before proposing any shortcuts.

        38.     The facts that the City’s Motion to Dismiss is pending and the Commission has

ordered EPE and Staff and allowed other parties to respond by July 21, 2026, factor into the

resolution of this motion, as well. The Commission might be well-advised to resolve that motion

and determine whether EPE must resubmit its Application in accordance with the future test year

period rate filing requirements of 17.1.3 NMAC before it deals with the issues raised by the Second

Errata Notice, which could become moot.

        39.     The Joint Movants understand that EPE’s request for an unprecedented increase in

base rates, coupled with the many issues about its rate case Application as filed, its proposed

changes in the Second Errata Notice, the Motion to Compel, and the discovery disputes of which

the City’s Motion to Compel may be just the first, would best be addressed and resolved in a

                                                   13
 holistic manner that is, quite frankly, not compatible with legal motions practice. The Joint

Movants firmly believe that the first step for the Commission should be to prevent this case from

getting even more convoluted by forcing Staff and the intervenors to file direct testimony by a date

before which some or most of these issues will be fully addressed, let alone resolved by the

Commission. The Joint Movants wish to express their desire to be helpful in reaching that broader

resolution, in the manner and timing chosen by the Commission.

       40.      Pursuant to 1.2.2.12(E)(1) NMAC, the City and the County have attempted to

determine whether this motion will be opposed by any of the parties to this proceeding. EPE

opposes the Motion because the Second Errata was filed for the benefit of Staff and Intervenors so

that they would have updated information in advance of the deadline for their direct testimony.

NMPRC Utility Division Staff takes no position on the motion at this time but reserves the right

to file a response. Western Resource Advocates does not oppose, the United States Department of

Defense and All Federal Executive Agencies do not oppose, Walmart, Inc. takes no position, and

New Mexico State University does not oppose. The City and County did not receive responses

from the other intervenors prior to filing this motion.

       WHEREFORE, the Joint Parties respectively move the Commission for:

       •     an expedited interim order staying the July 24, 2026, deadline for the filing of Staff and

             intervenor direct testimony;

       •     an order setting a deadline for responses to this motion that takes into consideration the

             other pending motions in this case as well as the later dates and deadlines in the

             Procedural Order and which requires EPE to provide a revised cost of service analysis
